burgers_1d_li2021.title: 1-D viscous Burgers, Li et al. (2021) operator-learning benchmark (1200 trajectories, 1024 points)
burgers_1d_li2021.description: u_t + (u^2/2)_x = nu u_xx on the periodic interval [0, 1), nu = 0.1, t in [0, 1]. Initial conditions u0 ~ N(0, 625 (-Laplacian + 25 I)^-2), the input distribution stated in Li et al. (2021), section 5.1 (their released generator used alpha 2.5, tau 7, sigma 49 instead; this dataset follows the paper's text). The standard task maps u0 to u(., 1); the 11 snapshots t = 0, 0.1, ..., 1 are stored for time-dependent models. Grid x_j = j / 1024, j = 0..1023; u[:, 0] equals u0.
burgers_1d_li2021.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20211
burgers_1d_li2021.verification: Solver (Fourier pseudo-spectral, 2/3 dealiasing, ETDRK4) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py against the Cole-Hopf exact solution (max error < 1e-8) and for exact mean conservation. Resolution and time-step study on 4 held-aside inputs against a reference with 4096 points and dt 2.5e-5, all 10 saved times: the dataset setting (1024 points, dt 1e-4) has max rel. L2 error 4.4e-12; halving dt gives 6.3e-13, doubling the points 4.4e-12 (time-step limited, spectrally converged in space). Mean conserved to 8e-17. Stored in float32 (rounding ~6e-8 relative), far below the 1e-3 to 1e-2 errors operator-learning methods reach on this task (scripts/zoo/operator_data.py convergence).
burgers_1d_li2021.citation: Li Z., Kovachki N., Azizzadenesheli K., Liu B., Bhattacharya K., Stuart A., Anandkumar A. (2021). Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations. ICLR 2021, arXiv:2010.08895. Data generated with PINNeAPPle's reference solvers (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

darcy_2d_li2021.title: 2-D Darcy flow, Li et al. (2021) operator-learning benchmark (1200 coefficient / pressure pairs, 128 x 128)
darcy_2d_li2021.description: -div(a grad u) = 1 on the unit square, u = 0 on the boundary. Coefficients a = 12 where g >= 0 and 3 where g < 0, g ~ N(0, (-Laplacian + 9 I)^-2) (Li et al. 2021, section 5.2). g is drawn as a periodic Gaussian random field on the 128 x 128 cell grid (Li et al. use a cosine expansion on 421 nodes), so a is piecewise constant on the cells of the stored grid. The task maps a to u. Cell centres ((i + 1/2) / 128, (j + 1/2) / 128); u is the cell average of the solution.
darcy_2d_li2021.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20212
darcy_2d_li2021.verification: Solver (cell-centred two-point-flux finite volumes, harmonic face coefficients, sparse direct solve) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py on a manufactured variable-coefficient solution (second order, max error < 2e-3 at 64^2). Each sample is solved on the 512^2 grid (the piecewise-constant coefficient is represented exactly on every refinement) and averaged onto its 128^2 cells. Grid study on 4 held-aside inputs against 1024^2: max rel. L2 error 4.6e-3 (128^2), 1.6e-3 (256^2), 4.3e-4 (512^2, the dataset); observed order 1.36 / 1.21 (reduced from 2 by the coefficient jumps); Richardson estimate of the dataset's discretisation error ~8e-4 rel. L2, ten times below the ~1e-2 operator-learning methods reach on this task. u > 0 and below the a = 3 bound 1/24 in every sample.
darcy_2d_li2021.citation: Li Z., Kovachki N., Azizzadenesheli K., Liu B., Bhattacharya K., Stuart A., Anandkumar A. (2021). Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations. ICLR 2021, arXiv:2010.08895. Data generated with PINNeAPPle's reference solvers (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.title: 2-D incompressible Navier-Stokes (vorticity), nu = 1e-3, Li et al. (2021) benchmark (1200 runs, 64 x 64, t 0-50)
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.description: w_t + u . grad w = nu Laplacian(w) + f on the periodic unit square, u = (psi_y, -psi_x), -Laplacian(psi) = w, nu = 1e-3, f(x, y) = 0.1 (sin 2 pi (x + y) + cos 2 pi (x + y)), w0 ~ N(0, 7^(3/2) (-Laplacian + 49 I)^-2.5) (Li et al. 2021, section 5.3). Solved on 128 x 128 and stored on the 64 x 64 grid x_i = i / 64 at t = 0, 1, ..., 50 (51 snapshots; w[:, 0] is w0). The usual task maps the first 10 snapshots to the next 40, or w0 to w(., 50).
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20213
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.verification: Solver (Fourier pseudo-spectral, 2/3 dealiasing, ETDRK4) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py: exact decay of a Taylor-Green vortex (1e-10) and a mean-free, finite forced flow. Resolution and time-step study on 4 held-aside inputs against a 256^2, dt 5e-3 reference at the stored 64^2 nodes and all 50 saved times: the dataset setting (128^2, dt 5e-2) has max rel. L2 error 4.0e-8 (6.6e-8 at t = 50); dt 2.5e-2 gives 2.5e-9 and dt 1e-2 6.0e-11 (fourth-order time convergence, the error is the time step's; the 128^2 grid is spectrally converged); solving directly on 64^2 would give 1.7e-4. Inputs are band-limited (Nyquist modes removed), so the 128^2 and 256^2 runs start from the same field. Every stored field is finite with spatial mean below 5e-8. Stored in float32 (~6e-8 relative), far below the 8e-3 or more operator-learning methods reach on this task.
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.citation: Li Z., Kovachki N., Azizzadenesheli K., Liu B., Bhattacharya K., Stuart A., Anandkumar A. (2021). Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations. ICLR 2021, arXiv:2010.08895. Data generated with PINNeAPPle's reference solvers (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

thermal_channel_cfd.title: Actuated heated-channel CFD, 2-D incompressible flow + heat (82 trajectories, 128 x 32, 101 snapshots)
thermal_channel_cfd.description: Non-dimensional channel [0, 10] x [0, 1], Re 100, Pr 0.71: parabolic inlet with time-varying mean velocity U(t) in [0.6, 1.4] and inlet temperature 0, no-slip walls, adiabatic except a heater on the bottom wall at x in [2, 4] with flux -dT/dy = Q(t) in [0, 2], zero-gradient outlet. After a 15-unit warm-up each trajectory records u, v, p, T on the 128 x 32 cell centres every 0.4 time units over 40 units (101 snapshots), with the actuators and the quantities of interest (bulk outlet temperature, maximum temperature, pressure drop, heat in / out, stored energy). Training actuation is random holds, steps and ramps; two test splits use families never seen in training (chirped sinusoids, steps between the range edges), for digital-twin and forecasting models. Cell centres and all solver settings are in meta.json; fields[:, k] is the state at t = 0.4 k.
thermal_channel_cfd.source: python scripts/zoo/thermal_channel_data.py generate --out DIR; recipe of PINNeAPPle-Benchmark experiment 05 (Apache-2.0) on pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_2d (staggered MAC grid, Chorin projection, dt 0.01), seeds per trajectory in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_datasets.PLAN
thermal_channel_cfd.verification: Solver checks (python scripts/zoo/thermal_channel_data.py verify, pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_datasets.verify): plane Poiseuille flow, max error of the velocity profile 4.8e-3 / 1.3e-3 / 3.5e-4 on 64 x 16 / 128 x 32 (the dataset grid) / 256 x 64 (second order), dp/dx within 1.2 % of -12/Re, max divergence 1e-7; fully developed Nusselt number for one wall at uniform flux and one adiabatic, 5.392 / 5.388 vs 5.385 exact (Shah & London 1978), global energy imbalance 2.7e-8. Three-grid study of an actuated run (64 x 16, 128 x 32, 256 x 64, dt halved with h): GCI of the dataset grid 3.7 % for the bulk outlet temperature (oscillatory convergence, observed order 1.3), 1.1 % for the maximum temperature (order 2.3), 1.3 % for the pressure drop (order 1.3). In every trajectory the change of stored energy matches the trapezoidal integral of the recorded heat in - out to 0.3 % (median, smooth actuation) and at most 4 % (steps, limited by the 0.4 sampling of the actuators). All fields finite; float32 storage.
thermal_channel_cfd.citation: PINNeAPPle-Benchmark experiment 05 (actuated heated channel). Data generated with PINNeAPPle (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_2d); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.
